message.content: {"caption":"A diagram contrasts an AI agent learning to optimize its own memory with a rigid, predefined memory strategy.","description":"The upper half shows a person with an open book pointing toward a learning panel titled “Teaching the Agent how to optimize memory.” A right-pointing blue arrow leads from the person to three lesson cards: “Understand goals,” “Learn to evaluate what to remember,” and “Learn to organize, update, and discard.” Another blue arrow points from the cards to a robot labeled “AGENT,” with a connected-node AI symbol above it. A dashed right-pointing arrow from the agent toward the checklist is labeled “Guided by principles.” Under “Agent optimizes its own memory,” four green checkmarks mark “Select important info,” “Compress and structure,” “Update and adapt,” and “Forget what’s unimportant.” Below the checklist, document icons are linked by lines to a blue database cylinder.\n\nThe bottom half compares two approaches. The left panel, “Previous Work: Give a Fish,” says “Force the model to follow a predefined memory strategy or format.” A clipboard labeled “Predefined Strategy / Format” points right along an arrow labeled “Force” to a robot; a second right-pointing arrow leads to a database cylinder labeled “Rigid Memory (hard to adapt).” A small brain-like thought symbol appears above the robot. “VS.” separates the panels. The right panel, “Our Principle: Teach to Fish,” says “Teach the model how to optimize its memory.” An open book labeled “Principles & Optimization Skills” points right to a robot, with a lightbulb symbol above it; a dashed right-pointing arrow leads from the robot to a database cylinder labeled “Flexible Memory (more adaptive).”","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
